Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Freight rework: fix it before the receiver rejects it. 

Receivers check five things: lean, torn wrap, overhang, broken pallets and pallet height. Any one of them can mean a receiver rejection, a return leg and a new delivery appointment. At Freitty, our crew reworks freight before delivery: pallet restack, rewrap, new pallets and height fixes, with photos before and after. 

Spotted one of the five on your load? Pull in to Freitty for freight rework and deliver on time.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Freight rework: fix it before the receiver rejects it. 

Receivers check five things: lean, torn wrap, overhang, broken pallets and pallet height. Any one of them can mean a receiver rejection, a return leg and a new delivery appointment. At Freitty, our crew reworks freight before delivery: pallet restack, rewrap, new pallets and height fixes, with photos before and after. 

Spotted one of the five on your load? Pull in to Freitty for freight rework and deliver on time.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Load securement supplies at Freitty: straps, corner protectors, dunnage bags. 

Most shifted loads come down to load securement. Straps hold the load on hard braking and sharp turns. Corner protectors stop straps from crushing the boxes. Dunnage bags fill the gaps so pallets can't slide. Freitty stabilizers, our own design, keep freight where it was loaded. 

Pick them up during your cross docking at Freitty or order online from the Freitty Shop.

Out of HOS? After-hours cross docking is your plan B for the load. 

200 miles to go and 45 minutes on your clock puts the appointment at risk. Freitty offers after-hours receiving: we take the load after closing, store it safely or reload it for the final leg. You take your 10-hour break, and the load recovery plan keeps the delivery on track. 

After-hours slots are booked ahead and prepaid. Book at Freitty before your hours run out.

Truck-to-truck transfer: trailer down, freight still on time. 

A breakdown stops the trailer, not the delivery. Bring the load to Freitty [City] and our crew does a truck-to-truck transfer: every pallet moved across the dock to a healthy trailer, with photos at unload and after loading. The freight keeps its schedule while the trailer goes to the shop. 

Book cross docking at Freitty online and keep your delivery window.

Freight rework: fix it before the receiver rejects it. 

Receivers check five things: lean, torn wrap, overhang, broken pallets and pallet height. Any one of them can mean a receiver rejection, a return leg and a new delivery appointment. At Freitty, our crew reworks freight before delivery: pallet restack, rewrap, new pallets and height fixes, with photos before and after. 

Spotted one of the five on your load? Pull in to Freitty for freight rework and deliver on time.

After-hours cross docking: back in tonight, not at 7 AM. 

Arriving after the dock closes usually means parking overnight and waiting for the morning crew. At Freitty, after-hours receiving lets you back in and start now. Our crew unloads, cross-docks and reloads your freight the same night, with photos at every step. A same-day transfer puts your truck back on the road tonight instead of nine hours at the gate. 

After-hours slots are booked ahead and prepaid. Book your cross dock at Freitty online in about 2 minutes.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Freight rework: fix it before the receiver rejects it. 

Receivers check five things: lean, torn wrap, overhang, broken pallets and pallet height. Any one of them can mean a receiver rejection, a return leg and a new delivery appointment. At Freitty, our crew reworks freight before delivery: pallet restack, rewrap, new pallets and height fixes, with photos before and after. 

Spotted one of the five on your load? Pull in to Freitty for freight rework and deliver on time.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Load securement supplies at Freitty: straps, corner protectors, dunnage bags. 

Most shifted loads come down to load securement. Straps hold the load on hard braking and sharp turns. Corner protectors stop straps from crushing the boxes. Dunnage bags fill the gaps so pallets can't slide. Freitty stabilizers, our own design, keep freight where it was loaded. 

Pick them up during your cross docking at Freitty or order online from the Freitty Shop.

Out of HOS? After-hours cross docking is your plan B for the load. 

200 miles to go and 45 minutes on your clock puts the appointment at risk. Freitty offers after-hours receiving: we take the load after closing, store it safely or reload it for the final leg. You take your 10-hour break, and the load recovery plan keeps the delivery on track. 

After-hours slots are booked ahead and prepaid. Book at Freitty before your hours run out.

Truck-to-truck transfer: trailer down, freight still on time. 

A breakdown stops the trailer, not the delivery. Bring the load to Freitty [City] and our crew does a truck-to-truck transfer: every pallet moved across the dock to a healthy trailer, with photos at unload and after loading. The freight keeps its schedule while the trailer goes to the shop. 

Book cross docking at Freitty online and keep your delivery window.

Freight rework: fix it before the receiver rejects it. 

Receivers check five things: lean, torn wrap, overhang, broken pallets and pallet height. Any one of them can mean a receiver rejection, a return leg and a new delivery appointment. At Freitty, our crew reworks freight before delivery: pallet restack, rewrap, new pallets and height fixes, with photos before and after. 

Spotted one of the five on your load? Pull in to Freitty for freight rework and deliver on time.

After-hours cross docking: back in tonight, not at 7 AM.

Our crew unloads, cross-docks and reloads your freight the same night, with photos at every step. A same-day transfer puts your truck back on the road tonight instead of nine hours at the gate. 

After-hours slots are booked ahead and prepaid. Book your cross dock at Freitty online in about 2 minutes.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

📦✅ 5 Steps of Efficient Cross-Dock Cargo Handling at Freitty 

Have you ever wondered what path your cargo takes during cross-docking? We’ve refined our workflow to ensure your goods are safe, documented with photos at every step, and ready to move.

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Overloaded hubs, truck shortages, rising rates, and delays can disrupt the entire supply chain. We’ve outlined the key risks and practical solutions to help you stay in control during peak periods.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.

Load securement supplies at Freitty: straps, corner protectors, dunnage bags. 

Most shifted loads come down to load securement. Straps hold the load on hard braking and sharp turns. Corner protectors stop straps from crushing the boxes. Dunnage bags fill the gaps so pallets can't slide. Freitty stabilizers, our own design, keep freight where it was loaded. 

Pick them up during your cross docking at Freitty or order online from the Freitty Shop.

Truck-to-truck transfer: trailer down, freight still on time. 

A breakdown stops the trailer, not the delivery. Bring the load to Freitty [City] and our crew does a truck-to-truck transfer: every pallet moved across the dock to a healthy trailer, with photos at unload and after loading. The freight keeps its schedule while the trailer goes to the shop.

Freight rework: fix it before the receiver rejects it. 

Receivers check five things: lean, torn wrap, overhang, broken pallets and pallet height. Any one of them can mean a receiver rejection, a return leg and a new delivery appointment. At Freitty, our crew reworks freight before delivery: pallet restack, rewrap, new pallets and height fixes, with photos before and after. 

Spotted one of the five on your load? Pull in to Freitty for freight rework and deliver on time.

Cross docking with photos at every step: your proof if a damage claim comes in. 

When a receiver reports damage, the driver often gets blamed for something that happened before or after his leg. At Freitty, every cross docking job comes with photo verification: pictures of the freight at unload and again once it is loaded and secured, sent to you before the truck leaves. Pallet count, condition and securement are all on record. 

If a damage claim comes in later, you have photos showing the condition of the load when it left our dock. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and keep a photo record of every load.

Cross docking: import container in, pallets out, same shift. 

Import containers are packed to fill the box, not to pass a receiver's dock check. The freight arrives floor-loaded or on pallets built for the ocean. At Freitty, cross docking handles that in one visit: our crew devans the container, builds pallets to the receiver's spec, wraps and photographs them, and loads the outbound trailer. No warehousing leg and no second building. 

Peak season makes this harder, because ships and DC appointments run on different schedules. A cross dock between the port and the DC closes that gap. 

Book cross docking at Freitty and send your import freight out on pallets.

Overweight Help: three dock fixes for an overweight load on drives. 

Over on the drives and under on the trailer axles often means the weight sits in the wrong place, not that the load is too heavy. At Freitty, our crew fixes it on the dock: 

Shift weight back. We move heavy pallets toward the trailer axles. 
Rebuild heavy pallets. A pallet restack makes tall, heavy stacks lower and more stable. 
Re-sequence the load. We weigh the pallets and reload them in the right order. 
Every fix comes with photos of the finished load, so you see how it was placed before the truck leaves. 

Overweight on your last scale ticket? Pull into Freitty for Overweight Help and roll out with the weight where it belongs.

Overweight Help: axle weight set right on the first load. 

Overweight on your drives means a second trip to the dock and another stop at the scale. At Freitty, we weigh the pallets before they go into the trailer, then place them so the weight sits right across the steer, drive and trailer axles. Our crews load around 60 pallets and 42,000 lbs in one pass, with fewer touches, less risk of damage and no mixed freight. 

Overweight Help can be added to any cross docking job at our hub, and you get photos of the finished load before it leaves the dock. 

Load already over on the drives? Book Overweight Help at Freitty and skip the second trip to the scale.
